name: internal-document-search-with-summaries
summary: Employees must find internal documents quickly and get a short summary without opening them.
goals: Clients read and write domain resources over HTTP.
The system notifies people through an external channel.
Files are uploaded, stored and served.
Scheduled jobs process stored records in windows.
Predictions are served from a versioned model.
Records are searched by meaning through embeddings.
Figures are aggregated over history for people to read.

rules: Type hints on every public function; dataclasses or pydantic for records.
No business logic in the HTTP layer.
Every component logs one structured line per unit of work with the correlation id.
No in-process state that a second instance would not see; instances are interchangeable.
Prefer the boring option; a new piece of infrastructure needs a decision record.
Python 3.12 as stated in the constraints.
Stateless processes: configuration from the environment, no local files that a second instance would not see.
definition_of_done: Acceptance checks of the package pass.
No file outside the write scope changed.
Every public operation of the implemented interfaces exists with the declared inputs.

requirements.statement: Employees must find internal documents quickly and get a short summary without opening them.
requirements.rationale: no catalogue pattern matched; owner chosen by the engine (see the notes)

requirements.statement: Employees upload PDF and Markdown documents (up to 20 MB) and tag them with a team.
The system extracts the text, splits it into chunks, computes embeddings and indexes them for semantic search.
Employees search with a natural-language query and get the ten best passages with links to the documents.
For each result the system generates a three-sentence summary with an LLM and caches it.
Team leads can delete documents; deleted documents disappear from search results within one minute.
Every search query is logged with the employee id for usage reporting; a weekly report is emailed to the knowledge team.
Search returns within 800 ms p95 for a corpus of 50,000 documents.
Embedding and summary generation must not block uploads; an upload is acknowledged within 1 s.
Documents are visible only to members of the tagged team.
requirements.rationale: no catalogue pattern matched; owner chosen by the engine (see the notes)

requirements.statement: Python 3.12, PostgreSQL with pgvector available, S3-compatible object storage available. Team of 3.
Embeddings and summaries come from an external API with a rate limit of 60 requests per minute.
Employees authenticate through the company SSO (OIDC).
Domain records are kept indefinitely; logs and audit history are retained for 1 year, after which a nightly job deletes them (assumed by the engine).

decisions.title: API style

options.name: GraphQL
cons: complexity budget for a small team

decisions.rationale: Scored against the active qualities; decided by durability (weight 1.0), availability (weight 0.9). REST/JSON over HTTP: 1.42; gRPC: 1.28; GraphQL: 1.14
decisions.consequences: Not choosing 'gRPC' gives up: typed contracts, streaming. Not choosing 'GraphQL' gives up: flexible queries.

decisions.title: Primary store
decisions.context: Domain records need durable, queryable storage.

options.name: MySQL / MariaDB (the stated database)
cons: weaker JSON and DDL ergonomics than PostgreSQL

options.name: Redis for the hot state (as stated) with a relational store for durable records
pros: the stated home of the hot data

options.name: Managed document store (DynamoDB/MongoDB, as stated)
cons: query patterns must be designed up front

decisions.rationale: Scored against the active qualities; decided by durability (weight 1.0), availability (weight 0.9). PostgreSQL: 3.30; SQLite: 1.61; Files: 1.16; MySQL / MariaDB: unavailable (needs mysql, not in the constraints); Redis for the hot state: unavailable (needs redis_primary, not in the constraints); Managed document store: unavailable (needs document_db, not in the constraints); In-memory: unavailable (ruled out by postgres, durable_required). stated in the constraints
decisions.consequences: Not choosing 'SQLite' gives up: zero operations, single file. Not choosing 'Files' gives up: no dependencies, human readable.

decisions.title: Caller authentication
decisions.context: Management operations must be attributable to a customer or operator.

options.name: API keys per customer, hashed at rest, sent as a bearer token
cons: no delegation or expiry unless added

options.name: OAuth2 / OIDC with the platform's identity provider
Session tokens issued by the platform's own account service to game/mobile clients (device-bound, short-lived, refreshable)
No account: a reference number plus a knowledge factor (date of birth) resumes a saved application; every attempt rate-limited and logged
pros: no credentials to manage for occasional users
cons: a reference number can be shared; scope what it unlocks

options.name: Email one-time code / magic link (no account needed)

decisions.choice: OAuth2 / OIDC with the platform's identity provider
decisions.rationale: Scored against the active qualities; decided by durability (weight 1.0), availability (weight 0.9). OAuth2 / OIDC with the platform's identity provi: 2.00; API keys per customer, hashed at rest, sent as a: 1.28; Mutual TLS: 0.86; Session tokens issued by the platform's own acco: unavailable (needs game_client, not in the constraints); No account: a reference number plus a knowledge : unavailable (needs no_account_auth, not in the constraints); Email one-time code / magic link: unavailable (needs email_auth, not in the constraints). stated in the constraints
decisions.consequences: Not choosing 'API keys per customer, hashed at rest, sent as a' gives up: simple, scriptable. Not choosing 'Mutual TLS' gives up: strong, no secrets in headers.

decisions.title: Caching
decisions.context: Repeated reads dominate the request mix.

options.name: Read-through cache with TTL and explicit invalidation on write
No cache; rely on database indexes

decisions.choice: Read-through cache with TTL and explicit invalidation on write
decisions.rationale: Scored against the active qualities; decided by durability (weight 1.0), availability (weight 0.9). Read-through cache with TTL and explicit invalid: 1.56; No cache: 1.56
decisions.consequences: Not choosing 'No cache; rely on database indexes' gives up: no staleness.

decisions.title: Process topology
decisions.context: The same code base serves requests and performs background work.

options.name: One image, role by flag: `api` and `worker` processes scale independently
pros: independent scaling of ingress and outbound work

options.name: Single process with background threads
cons: request latency competes with outbound work

options.name: Separate services per concern (ingest, admin, delivery)
cons: three deployables for a team of three

decisions.choice: One image, role by flag: `api` and `worker` processes scale independently
decisions.rationale: Scored against the active qualities; decided by durability (weight 1.0), availability (weight 0.9). One image, role by flag: `api` and `worker` proc: 2.10; Separate services per concern: 1.81; Single process with background threads: 1.42
decisions.consequences: Not choosing 'Separate services per concern' gives up: clear ownership. Not choosing 'Single process with background threads' gives up: one deployable.

decisions.title: Vector index for semantic search
decisions.context: Embeddings must be stored and searched by similarity.

options.name: pgvector in PostgreSQL
cons: ANN performance limits at tens of millions of vectors

options.name: Dedicated vector database
pros: scales to hundreds of millions of vectors
cons: sync with the source of truth

options.name: In-process index (FAISS/HNSW) rebuilt from the store

decisions.rationale: Scored against the active qualities; decided by durability (weight 1.0), availability (weight 0.9). pgvector in PostgreSQL: 2.70; In-process index: 1.56; Dedicated vector database: 1.28. stated in the constraints
decisions.consequences: Not choosing 'In-process index' gives up: fast, no service. Not choosing 'Dedicated vector database' gives up: scales to hundreds of millions of vectors.

decisions.title: Where reports are computed
decisions.context: Aggregations over history must not slow down the transactional path.

options.name: Materialised aggregates built by a scheduled job into report tables in the primary database
pros: reports are a read of precomputed rows

options.name: Read replica queried directly
cons: heavy queries still hit a copy of the OLTP schema

options.name: Columnar analytics store (ClickHouse / warehouse) fed by a pipeline
cons: a second store and a pipeline

decisions.choice: Materialised aggregates built by a scheduled job into report tables in the primary database
decisions.rationale: Scored against the active qualities; decided by durability (weight 1.0), availability (weight 0.9). Materialised aggregates built by a scheduled job: 1.82; Read replica queried directly: 1.54; Columnar analytics store: unavailable (needs clickhouse, not in the constraints)
decisions.consequences: Not choosing 'Read replica queried directly' gives up: fresh, no aggregate design.

decisions.title: Redundancy for the availability target
decisions.context: The availability target must be met through instance failures and deploys.

options.name: Two or more interchangeable instances per role behind the ingress, health checks, rolling deploys
cons: needs stateless instances and a shared store

decisions.choice: Two or more interchangeable instances per role behind the ingress, health checks, rolling deploys
decisions.rationale: Scored against the active qualities; decided by durability (weight 1.0), availability (weight 0.9). Two or more interchangeable instances per role b: 1.70; Active-active across two regions: 1.42; Single instance with health-based restart: 1.28
decisions.consequences: Not choosing 'Active-active across two regions' gives up: survives a regional outage. Not choosing 'Single instance with health-based restart' gives up: simplest, cheapest.

decisions.title: Assumed answer: stack (Q-deploy)
decisions.context: The requirements do not say. Question: Q-deploy. No evidence in the text; engine default.
decisions.rationale: The default for a networked service; keeps instances interchangeable.

risks.description: Payloads or uploads without size limits exhaust memory or disk.
risks.mitigation: Enforce size limits at the surface; reject early with a clear error.

risks.description: Entities evolve; migrations run against live data.
risks.mitigation: Versioned migrations applied before deploy; additive changes first, removals one release later.

risks.description: A widespread failure disables many targets and emails every owner at once.
risks.mitigation: Rate-limit notifications per owner and batch them.

risks.description: A management operation reachable without authentication.
risks.mitigation: Authenticate in one middleware for every management route; test every route unauthenticated.

risks.description: Dashboards show figures from a failed or late run without saying so.
risks.mitigation: Every report row carries the run's completion time; the UI shows it; alert when a run is late.

risks.description: Parts of the requirements were not recognised by the catalogue and received a generic decomposition.
risks.mitigation: Review the components marked generic; refine responsibilities and interfaces before briefing.
Parameterised queries only; no string-built SQL. Check: static check for string-formatted SQL finds nothing

risks.description: [information_disclosure] Store: Backups and dumps contain everything.
risks.mitigation: Encrypt backups; restrict who can take them. Check: backup file is not readable without the key

risks.description: [tampering] File storage: Uploaded content is not what its type claims.
risks.mitigation: Sniff content type; reject executables; size limits. Check: renamed executable is rejected

risks.description: [elevation] File storage: Path traversal through user-supplied names.
risks.mitigation: Generate storage keys; never use client names as paths. Check: name '../x' cannot escape the store

risks.description: [denial_of_service] Notifier: Notification storms and template injection.
risks.mitigation: Rate-limit per recipient; escape template context. Check: 1,000 failures produce one digest per owner

risks.description: [spoofing] Authentication: Credential stuffing or leaked keys.
risks.mitigation: Hash keys at rest; allow revocation; rate-limit failures. Check: revoked key is rejected within seconds; brute force is throttled

risks.description: [elevation] Authentication: A caller acts on another tenant's resources.
risks.mitigation: Every core operation takes the principal and checks ownership. Check: cross-tenant request returns 404/403 for every operation

risks.description: [denial_of_service] Model server: Adversarial or oversized inputs exhaust inference capacity.
risks.mitigation: Input size limits; batching with timeouts. Check: oversize input rejected before inference

risks.description: [information_disclosure] Reporting: Aggregates over small groups re-identify people.
risks.mitigation: Suppress rows below a minimum group size in person-level reports. Check: a report over a group of one shows no row

risks.description: [spoofing] Public HTTP API: Requests without a verified caller identity reach domain operations.
risks.mitigation: Authenticate every route in one middleware; deny by default. Check: every route returns 401 without credentials

risks.description: [tampering] Public HTTP API: Malformed or oversized bodies reach the core.
risks.mitigation: Schema-validate and size-limit at the surface; reject before parsing fully. Check: fuzz the body; oversize returns 413

risks.description: [denial_of_service] Public HTTP API: A single caller saturates the service.
risks.mitigation: Per-caller rate limit and request timeouts. Check: burst from one key returns 429; others unaffected

risks.description: [information_disclosure] Public HTTP API: Stack traces or internal ids leak in error responses.
risks.mitigation: Map exceptions to fixed error shapes; log details server-side only. Check: no traceback text in any 4xx/5xx body
